arguments.audience: private equity deal team and investment committee
arguments.brief: Proposal deck for Project Falcon: Meridian Capital Partners is considering acquiring Nordbolt, a European industrial fastener maker (revenue EUR 212M, EBITDA EUR 31M, 14.6% margin). We are pitching a 4-week commercial due diligence. Facts: the European fastener market grew from EUR 8.1bn (2021) to EUR 9.4bn (2025), forecast EUR 10.6bn by 2028; Nordbolt holds 2.3% share, number 6 in Europe; top three competitors are Bossard (9.1%), Wuerth (7.4%) and Fabory (3.8%). Nordbolt revenue by segment: automotive 41%, construction 27%, machinery 22%, other 10%. Margin bridge 2023 to 2025: 2023 EBITDA 24.0, price +6.5, volume +3.2, raw material -4.1, opex +1.4 = 31.0. Three scope options for the DD: (A) desktop-only market model, EUR 180k, 3 weeks; (B) market model plus 25 customer interviews, EUR 320k, 4 weeks; (C) B plus a channel-partner survey, EUR 410k, 5 weeks; we recommend B. Workplan (B): week 1 data room and market model, week 2 interviews wave 1, week 3 interviews wave 2 and synthesis, week 4 red-flag report and IC pack. Team: Anna Lindqvist (partner, 18 years industrials), Marco Rossi (manager, 3 prior fastener DDs), two consultants. Comparable: last year's DD on Project Keel (fastener distributor) found a 9-point price-gap risk that moved the bid by EUR 40M. Fees for B: market model 120k, interviews 140k, synthesis and IC pack 60k; an eight-line pricing schedule (phase, deliverable, days, fee). The ask: confirm scope B and sign the engagement letter by Friday. Required slides: market chart beside the 2.3% share number and position bullets; margin bridge waterfall beside a what-it-means narrative; Project Keel case with site photo and result metrics; two-column comparison B vs C; three-option evaluation matrix (cost, duration, confidence on price risk, confidence on volume risk); eight-row pricing schedule; team with headshot; next steps closer with the Friday ask.

slides.title: A four-week CDD can price the two risks that decide the Nordbolt bid

points.lead: Nordbolt is a sub-scale number six in a growing market.
points.support: EUR 212M revenue and 2.3% share of a EUR 9.4bn European fastener market heading to EUR 10.6bn by 2028.

points.lead: The margin story rests on price, which is the risk.
points.support: EBITDA rose from EUR 24.0M to 31.0M in two years; EUR 6.5M of that is price, taken while raw materials cost EUR 4.1M.

points.lead: Scope B tests price and volume with 25 customer voices.
points.support: A market model plus two interview waves in four weeks for EUR 320k; option C adds a channel survey for EUR 90k and a week.

points.lead: The ask: confirm scope B and sign the engagement letter by Friday.
points.support: That keeps the red-flag report and IC pack inside the exclusivity window.

slides.bottom_line: Confirm scope B by Friday: the IC pack lands in week four.

regions.heading: What this means for the bid
regions.body: Nearly all of the margin expansion came from price taken during a raw-material spike. If customers claw back even half of it when steel normalises, run-rate EBITDA falls by about EUR 3M and the multiple is paid on a number that does not hold.
bullets: Price durability is the first interview question
Volume added EUR 3.2M: real, if share held

slides.takeaway: The bid rests on whether EUR 6.5M of price sticks.

slides.title: On Project Keel the same test moved the bid by EUR 40M
slides.heading: A fastener distributor priced on a margin that did not hold
slides.body: Last year's commercial due diligence on Project Keel interviewed 22 customers of a European fastener distributor. The interviews showed the target's prices sat nine points above the market on its core SKUs and that two of its top five accounts were already re-tendering.
bullets: Price gap confirmed in both interview waves
Run-rate EBITDA restated before the IC
Bid lowered by EUR 40M and the deal still closed

slides.takeaway: Customer interviews, not the data room, found the gap.
